title: Smithsonian American Women's History Museum Act
official_title: To permit the Smithsonian American Women's History Museum to be located within the Reserve of the National Mall, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: The underlying museum-site designation had 231 cosponsors, but the provisions limiting the museum to biological women, barring depiction of any biological male as a female, and mandating political-viewpoint representation drew enough opposition to block the bill in the House. Advancing a version would require dropping or softening those provisions.
summary: This bill sets the location of the future Smithsonian American Women's History Museum at a site on the National Mall and clears the way for the Smithsonian to build there. It also limits the museum's subject to the history of biological women and requires its exhibits to represent a range of political viewpoints.
brief: Designates a National Mall site for the Smithsonian American Women's History Museum and limits its mission to the history of biological women.

top_lines.headline: National Mall Site Designation
subs: Designates the South Monument site on the National Mall
President may choose an alternative site within 180 days
Transfers the land's jurisdiction to the Smithsonian

top_lines.headline: Museum Mission Scope
subs: Limits the museum to the history of biological women
Bars depicting any biological male as a female

top_lines.headline: Exhibit Content and Reporting
subs: Requires equal representation of diverse political viewpoints
Reports to Congress within 120 days, then every 2 years

items.main: Designates the South Monument site on the National Mall as the museum's location, with the President able to designate an alternative site within 180 days.
items.detail: The site is bordered by 14th Street Southwest, Jefferson Drive Southwest, Raoul Wallenberg Place Southwest, and Independence Avenue Southwest. The provision authorizes siting the museum within the Reserve of the National Mall by striking a prior exception clause in Section 107(d) of division T of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021.

items.main: Requires the federal agency holding the land to transfer administrative jurisdiction to the Smithsonian Institution and allows construction of a museum building.
items.detail: The Board of Regents may plan, design, and construct the building with approval from the Commission of Fine Arts, the National Capital Planning Commission, and the National Capital Memorial Advisory Commission. The Smithsonian must reimburse the land-holding agency within 60 days for costs from the approval process.

items.main: Sets the museum's mission scope to the history, achievements, and lived experiences of biological women, and prohibits depicting any biological male as a female.
items.detail: The provision adds a 'Scope of Mission' subsection to Section 103 of division T of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021. It states the museum may not identify, present, describe, or otherwise depict any biological male as a female.

items.main: Requires the museum's Council to ensure exhibits and programs reflect equal representation of diverse political viewpoints among women.
items.detail: The Council must seek guidance from a 'broad array' of knowledgeable and respected sources reflecting varied political ideologies, cultures, and lived experiences. The Secretary of the Smithsonian must report to seven House and Senate committees within 120 days of enactment and every 2 years thereafter on compliance.

underreported.summary: Restricts the museum's subject matter to biological women and prohibits it from depicting any biological male as a female.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill's title and headline concern permitting the museum's location on the National Mall, but this subsection defines the museum's mission content rather than its site.

underreported.section: Section 2(e) - Ensuring Diversity of Political Viewpoints
underreported.summary: Requires the Council to ensure exhibits and programs give equal representation to the diversity of political viewpoints held by women.
underreported.why_unreported: This imposes an ongoing content requirement on the museum's exhibits, an effect not implied by a bill framed around the museum's physical location.

criticisms.why: I stand proudly to support H.R. 1329, the bipartisan Smithsonian American Women's History Museum Act, as an original cosponsor. For 30 years, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have worked together to establish a space that carries on the legacy of the American women who fought tirelessly for our rights. It is absolutely unacceptable that any Member would oppose this bill because they want a biological male, a man, to be honored in the space designed for women, biological women.

gaps: The bill designates the South Monument site and authorizes constructing a building but does not identify a funding source or construction cost for the museum.
The bill prohibits depicting any biological male as a female but does not define 'biological male' or 'biological female.'
The bill requires exhibits to give equal representation to diverse political viewpoints but does not define how equal representation is measured.
The bill mandates biennial compliance reports to Congress but specifies no consequence if the museum does not comply.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. De La Cruz
featured_quotes.text: I stand proudly to support H.R. 1329, the bipartisan Smithsonian American Women's History Museum Act, as an original cosponsor. For 30 years, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have worked together to establish a space that carries on the legacy of the American women who fought tirelessly for our rights. It is absolutely unacceptable that any Member would oppose this bill because they want a biological male, a man, to be honored in the space designed for women, biological women.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Cammack
featured_quotes.text: I appreciate my colleague from the great State of Wisconsin for his leadership on this issue. As you can see, I have my daughter, Augusta Dair, here with me today because I wanted her to be a witness to this incredible moment in our Nation's history where we stood up for all of the women who have helped build this country and told their stories. That is what this museum is. It is not a political statement. It is a promise, a promise that the women who came before us will not be erased, will not be minimized, and will not be forgotten.
